newsitem.title: USA: K-III to sell New Woman magazine to Rodale.
newsitem.headline: K-III to sell New Woman magazine to Rodale.

text.p: Rodale Press has agreed to acquire New Woman magazine from K-III Communications Corp, the companies said Monday. Terms were not disclosed.
Rodale will publish New Woman beginning with the November 1997 issue, the companies said in a joint statement.

New Woman's circulation of one million, and advertising base of 1,000 pages, create a perfect synergy with other Rodale publications such as Men's Health (1.3 million circulation) and Prevention (3.2 million), the companies said.

The divestiture of New Woman will mark the third recent divestiture of one of K-III's non-core businesses, said Warren Bimblick, K-III vice president-investor relations. K-III has also sold its Katharine Gibbs secretarial and business schools and Krames, a publisher of medical information, he said.
K-III is focusing on specialty media, including technical and trade magazines, education, and consumer and business directories, Bimblick said.
K-III plans to divest the Daily Racing Form and Newbridge Book Clubs, he said.
Proceeds to K-III from the New Woman sale will be used for general corporate purposes and debt reduction, Bimblick said.
Rodale magazine division president John Griffin said in a statement that beginning with the November issue, New Woman will no longer be accepting cigarette or hard liquor advertising.
Last year, this element of advertising accounted for less than 10 percent of New Woman's advertising base, the company said.
Griffin said Rodale plans to maintain the magazine at its current location in New York.
